# PDF regression fixtures

These fixtures are deterministic, minimal PDF 1.4 files generated by [`scripts/generate_pdf_fixtures.py`](../../../scripts/generate_pdf_fixtures.py). They contain synthetic text only—never customer PDFs, passwords, signatures, OCR models, or other sensitive content.

| Fixture | Contract | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `single-page-text.pdf` | One page containing `PDF Seeker Fixture: single-page text` | Load, text extraction, and edit-output reopen checks |
| `three-page-target.pdf` | Three pages with ordered target labels | Page rotation and insert-pages target |
| `two-page-source.pdf` | Two pages with ordered source labels | Insert-pages source |
| `rotated-contents-array.pdf` | One 90°-rotated page whose `/Contents` is an array of two streams | Content-array preservation, rotation, reopen, and render checks |
| `two-by-two-rgba.png` | Tiny 2×2 RGBA image with four distinct colors | Image-to-PDF embedding and output reopen |
| `truncated-input.pdf` | Deliberately truncated PDF header/object data | Safe failure and no final output |

The Rust regression tests copy fixtures into a temporary directory before invoking commands because input path validation requires existing canonical paths. Output paths are intentionally nonexistent before the command runs, matching normal Save As behavior; the tests reopen every generated PDF with `lopdf`.

## Updating the corpus

```bash
python3 scripts/generate_pdf_fixtures.py
cd src-tauri && cargo test
```

Keep fixtures small, deterministic, and legally redistributable. Add a fixture only when it represents a distinct PDF contract that a regression test verifies.
